title: Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC held Marshall’s complaint judicially out of order because his objections in the judicial case belonged in an appeal and an appeal was already pending. It awarded no relief on the complaint’s merits.
first_summary: Marshall challenged Pacific Presbytery’s refusal to dismiss a judicial case for alleged procedural irregularities. The SJC rejected his complaint as judicially out of order because those objections belonged in an appeal and his appeal was already pending.
summary: Marshall complained that Pacific Presbytery wrongly refused to dismiss a judicial case despite alleged procedural irregularities in the indictment and process. The SJC held the complaint judicially out of order: objections arising in a judicial case were to be preserved for appeal under BCO 32-14 and 42-3, and Marshall’s pending appeal independently barred a complaint under BCO 43-1. It granted no complaint relief. Separate opinions disputed the first rationale but agreed that the pending appeal barred the complaint.

sources.supports: Case identity, adopted SJC decision, judicially-out-of-order ruling, reasons, and vote.
Procedural dispute and separate opinion’s agreement with the result but disagreement with the first rationale.

evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The operative judgment declares the complaint judicially out of order under BCO 32-14, 42-3, and 43-1 at printed p. 548, line 19.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The separate opinions agree that the pending appeal barred the complaint but question or reject the judgment’s first rationale; printed p. 550, lines 110–115, and pp. 553–554, lines 170–232.

source_limits: The operative judgment is brief. Most factual history and criticism of one rationale come from separate opinions, not adopted findings.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged refusal to dismiss based on alleged indictment and process irregularities.
score_reasons.decision: States the complaint was judicially out of order and received no merits relief.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Preserves both adopted grounds, including the independently sufficient pending-appeal bar.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Explains that objections in a judicial case belong in appeal and cannot proceed concurrently by complaint once an appeal is pending.
score_reasons.fidelity: Clearly distinguishes the operative judgment from separate opinions and allegations.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the procedural ruling and qualification.
